title: What the Wrong Answers Showed Me
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] After every practice test, I used to check the score, feel happy or disappointed, and close the book. I rarely looked at the questions again.
Narrator: My teacher said the score measured one attempt, but the mistakes could guide the next week of study.
Narrator: [reflective] She gave us a simple error log with four columns: question, my answer, correct reason, and next action.
Narrator: At first, the process felt slow. I wanted to move directly to another test and prove that I could score higher.
Narrator: [honestly] When I filled the log, I noticed a pattern. Most vocabulary errors came from choosing a familiar-looking word without reading the whole sentence.
Narrator: My listening errors were different. I understood the topic, but I missed numbers, dates, and negative words such as “not” or “never.”
Narrator: [encouraged] These patterns needed different solutions. For vocabulary, I began underlining context words before choosing.
Narrator: For listening, I wrote short symbols for important details and checked whether a speaker corrected earlier information.
Narrator: [determined] One grammar mistake came from a rule I had never understood. I took it to the teacher instead of calling it a careless error.
Narrator: Two weeks later, I completed another practice test. My score improved, but the most useful result was that my new errors were easier to explain.
Narrator: [warmly] I no longer saw every red mark as the same kind of failure. Some showed missing knowledge, some showed rushed reading, and some showed a weak strategy.
Narrator: The log also stopped me from repeating easy exercises only because they felt comfortable.
Narrator: [hopeful] Now I review old errors before choosing new study material. The review takes fifteen minutes and gives my practice a clear direction.
Narrator: A wrong answer is not automatically useful. It becomes useful when we identify why it happened and choose a specific response.
Narrator: [gently] The test ends when time is called, but learning from it can begin afterward.

quiz.question: What did the narrator used to do after a test?
options: Check the score and close the book
quiz.explanation: The old routine ended with the score.

quiz.question: What four parts were in the error log?
options: Question, answer, reason, and next action
quiz.explanation: The log connected each error with a response.

quiz.question: What caused many vocabulary mistakes?
options: Choosing a familiar word without full context

quiz.question: How were listening mistakes different?
options: Details such as numbers and negatives were missed
quiz.explanation: He understood topics but lost key details.

quiz.question: When does a wrong answer become useful?
options: When its cause and response are identified
Only when the score is high
quiz.explanation: Analysis turns an error into study direction.

quiz.question: Why was checking only the score insufficient?
options: It measured performance without guiding the next study action
quiz.explanation: Mistakes carried diagnostic information the number alone lacked.

quiz.question: What pattern linked vocabulary errors?
options: Familiar-looking words were chosen without sentence context

quiz.question: Why did listening require a different solution?
options: The narrator could not hear anything
Topic understanding was present, but precise details were missed
quiz.explanation: The error type called for detail notation and correction awareness.

quiz.question: Why take one grammar item to the teacher?
options: The log had no grammar column
It reflected missing understanding rather than simple carelessness
The test score was too high

quiz.question: What made later errors more useful even before perfect scores?
options: They were all the same type
Their causes were easier to explain and address
quiz.explanation: Clear diagnosis improved control of future practice.
